newsitem.title: JAPAN: Anti-war Japan film director Kobayashi dies.
newsitem.headline: Anti-war Japan film director Kobayashi dies.

text.p: Masaki Kobayashi, a noted film director known for his anti-war themes, died of cardiac arrest at his Tokyo home, Japanese newspapers reported on Saturday. He was 80.

Kobayashi is best known for his three-part, nine-and-half hour movie "Ningen No Joken" (The Human Condition) released during 1959-1961. The film depicts a conscientious Japanese man who gets trapped in the Japanese Army's brutal exploits in China and dies while trying to flee from a Soviet concentration camp.
Kobayashi won special awards at the Cannes International Film Festival in 1963 for "Seppuku" (Harakiri) and in 1965 for "Kaidan" (Kwaidan), both which challenged Japan's social inconsistencies.
In 1982, he released a documentary called "Tokyo Saiban" (The Tokyo War Crimes Tribunal) that depicted the path of Japan's aggression in Asia until the end of World War Two.
Kobayashi graduated from Tokyo's Waseda University and joined Shochiku Studios in 1941, but was drafted into the army the following year.

In 1945, he was taken prisoner on Japan's southern Okinawa island, an experience recounted in his film "Kabe Atsuki Heya" (The Thick Walled Room) about junior officer scapegoats tried as war criminals, in 1953.
